Neovim 0.12+ is now required

hey there everyone! from now on, we have decided to raise the minimum neovim version to 0.12+ in #3588. this also applies when using WSL or connecting to a remote neovim server. If you need an older neovim version, use an earlier Neovide release that supports it.

Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-codex ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v0.21.44 Stable2026-10-31T12:15:10Z

oh-my-codex v0.21.44

Summary

This patch release fixes the native runtime hydration timeout/abort path reported in #3968.

Fixed

  • NATIVE RUNTIME HYDRATION (#3977): Increase postinstall hydration's timeout from 15 seconds to 120 seconds. Timed-out hydration now reports an explicit timeout and underlying error context with diagnostic URLs redacted.
  • FOREGROUND RECOVERY: Add omx native-runtime hydrate to retry hydration in the foreground and report failures. For the affected unsupported Process identity readiness state, omx doctor recommends this command and retains the session-pointer recovery note.
  • ACTIONABLE ASSET ERRORS: Include sanitized manifest and archive URLs and underlying fetch/read errors in native asset hydration diagnostics.

The fix addresses the hydration timeout/abort path; it does not claim to eliminate unrelated causes of native Process identity provider unavailability.

Compatibility

No breaking API changes. Release-coupled metadata was already synchronized to 0.21.44 on dev by #3976; the release does not bump those surfaces again.

Verification

  • npm ci — passed.
  • npm run build — passed.
  • npm test — passed, including runtime build/tests, the Node test suite, generated catalog checks, and prompt-invariant checks.
  • npm run check:no-unused — passed.
  • npm run lint — passed across 900 files; Biome reported the existing linter.rules.recommended deprecation notice.

Contributors

Thanks to @Yeachan-Heo for contributing to this release.

alam00000/bentopdf ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v2.8.11Measurement Tools and A Year of BentoPDF! - v2.8.11 Stable2026-10-31T11:31:39Z

Dad Joke Of the Release

Why don't skeletons fight each other? Because they don't have the guts 🤣

BentoPDF Is One Year Old! 🎉

I didn't realize this. The first release of BentoPDF, v1.0.0, went out on 20 October 2025, which means BentoPDF is now one year old! I'm so thankful to every one of you who used it, shared it, reported bugs, translated it and sent PRs. None of this would have happened without you. ❤️

Also I need your support to keep going

BentoPDF has grown into a lot more than one tool, but behind it there is still just one core maintainer: me. Every feature, every engine, every bug fix, every PR review and every issue reply goes through one person, and keeping this pace up on my own is getting really hard.

Your support goes directly into:

  • BentoPDF, with faster releases and faster fixes
  • Kura, our PDF standards and preflight engine
  • Hyper Compress, our compression engine
  • BentoParse, our new document parsing engine
  • Hiring a second core maintainer to work full time on BentoPDF, so the project no longer depends on just one person

Here's how you can help:

  1. Sponsor on GitHub Sponsors. Monthly sponsorships make the biggest difference, even small ones, because they let me plan ahead. You can also chip in once on Ko-fi.
  2. Advertise on bentopdf.com. The homepage now has a sponsor section right above the tools. The last time we had analytics, bentopdf.com was getting around 20,000 views a day, and it's very likely more now (we removed Simple Analytics, so we can't say for sure). Ads are plain logos and links: no tracking, no scripts and no pop-ups, and self-hosted copies never show them. Book a slot at bentopdf.com/advertise.
  3. Get a commercial license if your company uses BentoPDF and doesn't want the AGPL obligations. See bentopdf.com/licensing.

Every sponsor, every ad and every license helps keep BentoPDF free and private for everyone. Even if you can't, thank you for using it! ❤️

Alright, so back on to the release.

1. Measurement Tools

BentoPDF can now measure directly on your PDFs. Open any PDF in the PDF Editor, switch to Measure tab.

  • Distance, Perimeter and Area tools for floor plans, drawings, maps and anything else drawn to scale
  • Set the scale by typing it in, or calibrate it by clicking two points of a length you already know
  • Scale areas: give different parts of a page their own scale, for drawings that have several views or details on one sheet. Scales already saved inside a PDF are picked up automatically
  • Snapping to the drawing itself: endpoints, midpoints, intersections and along lines. Shapes snap together cleanly, so a new area can start exactly on the corner of another one
  • Magnifier: a loupe follows your cursor and zooms in on the spot you're measuring, so you can place points precisely on small details. You can turn it off from the Measure toolbar
  • Units: in, ft, yd, mi, mm, cm, m, km and pt, with decimal or fractional precision (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16)
  • Saved as standard PDF measurement data, so your measurements stay with the file

2. Favorite Tools

Star the tools you use most and they get pinned to a Favorites section at the top of the homepage. On mobiles, hold the tool card to favorite.

3. PDF Multi Tool Revamp

The PDF multi tool has been redesigned for a cleaner interface, and can now handle very large PDFs, upto 10k pages even, with ease.

  • Insert pages from a file, a blank page, pages from the clipboard, or Alternate Merge to interleave another PDF's pages before or after each page
  • Cut, copy, paste, duplicate and replace pages
  • Extract pages as a new PDF or as images
  • Split into multiple PDFs by page range, even and odd pages, one per page, every N pages, bookmarks (choose the depth) or maximum file size
  • Page Numbering, with style, prefix and starting number for any range
  • Page Size, to change page dimensions. Also automatically detects uneven page sizes
  • Reverse the page order
  • Rotate, delete and drag to reorder, one page or many at once
  • Thumbnail size control

4. Compress PDF Now Runs On Hyper Compress

Hyper Repo

Compress PDF now uses Hyper Compress, our own compression engine, which is the best open source PDF compressor btw, instead of the old pipeline. Pick Low, Medium, High or Lossless. The older, Photon and Condense are deprecated and Hyper handles everything.

v0.12.0CCFA-Skills v0.12.0 · GPT6适配版 Stable2026-10-31T06:37:51Z

CCFA-Skills 0.12.0：让长任务接得住，让每次修改都落到结果上。

本版保留18个skills、Humanization→Common前置、原有十项个性化设置与研究分工，集中修复实际使用中的断点。

本次更新

  • 写作与上下文：精简五个入口；两项强制前置从19,146降至10,174字符。按任务读取细节，保留真实原文学习、技术含义、必要不确定性和句尾意义。长稿带着全文主线、目标与邻段修改，并检查版本和修改范围。
  • 独立专家审读：沿用独立复核开关，用简短提示与全新上下文安排真实可用的GPT-6实例。新增中性问题、范围、排除项和材料位置；按实际运行配置与规则身份判断能否复用，主审整合为原有报告。
  • 科研执行与RSI：显式复测已有候选，共享跨分支预算；检查声明依赖和环境身份，支持低开销状态读取。最终确认绑定冻结候选与独立任务身份，只记录结果，不参与选优。
  • 绘图：按样本ID连接配对数据，组合推荐检查字段和排除条件；字号贯通模板与联动布局，补齐macOS及Linux CJK字体支持。保留43图法、九套原模板、用户参考组合和旧示例。
  • 安装与更新：提供轻量包和可选完整论文PDF包，逐文件SHA-256校验；全量/部分安装包含所需相邻资源，识别个人修改，保留用户额外文件与偏好。源码仍提供完整论文资源。

下载与安装

  • ccfa-skills-0.12.0-lean.zip：推荐安装，约61.6 MB，包含技能、原文文本、绘图库与模板。
  • ccfa-skills-0.12.0-papers.zip：可选离线原始论文PDF，约270.2 MB，包含34份PDF。
  • SHA256SUMS：下载校验值。

解压后使用包内 tools/install_release.py，显式指定源目录与客户端skills目录；可先使用--dry-run。完整步骤见仓库安装矩阵。安装后开启新会话。

验收

  • 本地502项回归无失败，3项Windows符号链接权限跳过；绘图261项、研究运行48项、专家请求27项均通过。
  • GitHub CI的Linux完整检查、Windows与macOS安装/Unicode烟雾检查均通过。
  • 三个版本各完成4个真实内容任务，共12份回答，事实与技术词均保留；一次独立盲评未区分出本组任务的质量差距。
  • 入口字符缩减是已测结构变化，不等于实测模型token节省。小样输出与方法已随仓库公开。

Install

Windows

Zip

  1. Download nvim-win64.zip (or nvim-win-arm64.zip for ARM)
  2. Extract the zip
  3. Run nvim.exe in your terminal

MSI

  1. Download nvim-win64.msi (or nvim-win-arm64.msi for ARM)
  2. Run the MSI
  3. Run nvim.exe in your terminal

Note: On Windows "Server" you may need to install vcruntime*.dll.

macOS (x86_64)

  1. Download nvim-macos-x86_64.tar.gz
  2. Run xattr -c ./nvim-macos-x86_64.tar.gz (to avoid "unknown developer" warning)
  3. Extract: tar xzvf nvim-macos-x86_64.tar.gz
  4. Run ./nvim-macos-x86_64/bin/nvim

macOS (arm64)

  1. Download nvim-macos-arm64.tar.gz
  2. Run xattr -c ./nvim-macos-arm64.tar.gz (to avoid "unknown developer" warning)

  4. Run ./nvim-macos-arm64/bin/nvim

Linux (x86_64)

If your system does not have the required glibc version, try the (unsupported) builds for older glibc.

AppImage

  1. Download nvim-linux-x86_64.appimage
  2. Run chmod u+x nvim-linux-x86_64.appimage && ./nvim-linux-x86_64.appimage
    • If your system does not have FUSE you can extract the appimage:
      ./nvim-linux-x86_64.appimage --appimage-extract
./squashfs-root/usr/bin/nvim

./squashfs-root/usr/bin/nvim

v0.8.222 Stable2026-10-30T18:33:49Z

HyperFrames v0.8.222

Released on 2026-10-30.

Render takes --start and --end to make just one span of the film as its own MP4. Capture retries without WebGL when a page stops answering, so more exports finish. Lint warns when a font or image in a linked stylesheet points at the wrong folder.

Features

  • Lint: Warn when a url() in a linked stylesheet does not resolve beside it (6cddd1a24, #6844).
  • Telemetry: Render_complete splits capture time into seek, page, screenshot and encoder wait (4da50e221, #6839).
  • CLI: Render --start and --end render only that span of the film as its own MP4 (5a164fb36, #6834).
  • CLI: Review notes name the command that reviews the cuts inside a sub-composition (01783f375, #6820).
  • CLI: Beats analyses an audio or video file given directly (a37307126, #6812).

Fixes

  • CLI: History show --diff names a changed video or audio file instead of refusing (4ba01be15, #6836).
  • CLI: Point a brace-stripped JSON flag value at the file and stdin forms (3ebf888fb, #6838).
  • Producer: Render telemetry names content gates instead of calling them disabled (6a8c064fb, #6835).
  • CLI: --variables-file and --variables <path> read the file again (6f2b07227, #6831).
  • Lint: A font the project's root stylesheet declares counts for its sub-compositions (bf4717893, #6827).
  • CLI: Capture retries without WebGL when the page stops answering under software GL (ef2159fe8, #6821).
  • Studio: A split at a clip's edge leaves the file unchanged (b20d0a62c, #6826).
  • CLI: Check and snapshot load GSAP from the bundled copy, not jsDelivr (88d8e5b49, #6824).
  • CLI: Check drops a request a network change cut when the file loads again (44ee07a2d, #6823).
  • Producer: Report extract_video progress while ffmpeg extracts frames (536209da0, #6822).
  • CLI: Check no longer calls text occluded by a cover that a CSS mask paints through (d4a866d61, #6818).
  • CLI: Render names the FFmpeg that has no libx264 and how to point at another (315969cda, #6819).
  • CLI: Check sees an image swap even when the page cannot read the image's pixels (054592c4d, #6817).
  • Producer: A render that stalls before its first frame says which worker phase it was in (2f8b8c47e, #6814).
  • Engine: A video clip starting between frames shows its media on the right frame (10a4ed56c, #6759).
  • CLI: The ignored-binary note names only the missing binary, and covers .hyperframes/bin (71b668010, #6807).
  • CLI: Add says --dir is the project root when the folder is missing (0bd1fd597, #6808).
  • Core: The first cut after Play starts on time instead of running ahead (07c714ce9, #6794).

@oh-my-pi/pi-agent-core

Breaking Changes

  • SentToolDefinitions.inactiveFor(messages, tools) is replaced by withInactiveTools(context), which also clears a stale inactiveTools; transformProviderContext now receives the request's inactiveTools (#17492)

Fixed

  • Long tool-call intents no longer block tool execution when intent tracing is enabled (#13140).

@oh-my-pi/pi-ai

Added

  • Added the codexAccessPrograms stream option and configureCodexAccessPrograms() process default to turn off the automatic Daybreak Blue access_programs request on Codex (#17508 by @H4vC)
  • Added waitForSibling to RotateCredentialOptions; set it to false to skip the short sibling-unblock wait in limits.rotate() while still blocking the failed credential (#17439 by @wolfiesch)

Changed

  • Cursor runs served through omp auth-gateway are limited to the client's own tools, all advertised as MCP; Cursor's built-in tools (file, shell, edit, todo, web fetch, SCM) are no longer offered on that path (#17382 by @eggpeat)

Fixed

  • Fixed native judgment requests (TypeSafe, OpenRouter Decisions, OpenAI Decisions, Workers AI) sending credentials in their state unredacted while credential redaction was on (#17443)
  • Fixed every new Codex session, including each subagent, losing a response and retrying when the native turn lane refuses live steering; once refused, later sessions on the same account, endpoint, and model queue follow-ups for four hours (#14158, #17438 by @wolfiesch)
  • Fixed Cursor models served through omp auth-gateway being told their file and shell tools were unavailable while the client ran the calls anyway, in Cursor's own argument shape (edits failed validation); each call now reaches the client as one of its own tools and the turn stops with toolUse until the result comes back (#17382 by @eggpeat)
  • Fixed Cursor models served through omp auth-gateway being told each tool call was handed off, which left Composer issuing calls blind and answering their results with empty stops; the gateway now keeps the Cursor run open while the client runs a step's calls and answers them in-band with the client's results on its next request (up to 30 minutes; otherwise the turn is rebuilt from history as before) (#17382 by @eggpeat)
  • Fixed Anthropic-compatible endpoints behind a relay opening a new connection for every turn: the response body is now drained for up to 2.5 s after message_stop instead of being cancelled, so the kept-alive connection is reused (#17432 by @flosrn)

@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog

Changed

  • Clamping a requested thinking effort now resolves through the model's effortMap alias first, so the request lands on the tier the model serves instead of the nearest lower one (#17395 by @Maziar123)
  • Long image-heavy conversations on the official Anthropic API now keep up to 120 MB of inline images before evicting older ones, following the Messages API request limit increase from 32 MB to 128 MB
  • The official Anthropic API now records its 128 MB request limit (request-body-byte-limit), so the newest message's images can use the 8 MB reserve and long text cannot push images past the limit (#17492 by @will-bogusz)

Fixed

  • Fixed Cursor's DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 reporting zero cost; every effort level now bills at Cursor's API rate of $0.30/$1.20 per million tokens, with cache reads at $0.006 (#17390 by @eggpeat)

@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent

Added

  • Added the providers.openai-codex.daybreak setting (default on) to stop omp from automatically requesting the Daybreak Blue cyber access program on eligible ChatGPT accounts; each session follows its own value (#17508 by @H4vC)
  • Added queueable compaction: /compact sent with the follow-up key (Ctrl+Q) while the agent works now runs when it yields instead of interrupting it (#17397 by @H4vC)
  • Added omp session lease [--json] -- <session-id>... and the RPC command get_session_lease, which report which sessions a running omp owns ({"held": [...], "unknown": [...]}) without taking ownership, so another program can check a session without forking it (#17428 by @andrebrait)
  • Added opt-in title.refreshAfterPrompts: every N operator prompts, the judge model checks whether a generated session title still fits the conversation and regenerates it when it does not; user-set titles are never replaced (#17443 by @wolfiesch)
  • Gateway rows discovered from /v1/models now keep the reasoning_effort_map and reasoning_required facts they advertise: a route that serves only low/high/max routes medium to high instead of the nearest lower tier, and a thinking-off request still sends a tier the route accepts (#17395 by @Maziar123)
  • Computer-use scripts can wait for a window opened by an action and read it in the same call with a window filter's optional wait (#17391 by @will-bogusz)

Changed

  • read of a web page keeps the title, description, author and dates of its <meta> tags and lists the others by name only, so pages cost about 6% fewer tokens (#17393 by @will-bogusz)
  • On the Anthropic API, the newest message now keeps all its images up to the 128 MB request limit, past the 120 MB image budget (#17492 by @will-bogusz)

Fixed

  • Fixed account-policy recovery repeatedly rotating through denied credentials instead of surfacing the error or using the configured model fallback, including unnecessary sibling-unblock waits after the account allowance is spent (#17439 by @wolfiesch)
  • Startup prewalk now arms a later fallback candidate of the role named by prewalk.into when its first candidate is unavailable, matching /prewalk and /new (#17373).
  • Fixed omp install git:github.com/user/repo treating git as the host instead of installing the GitHub plugin (#17436).
  • Fixed read showing a zip, tar, asar or ISO archive's old contents after a same-size rewrite within milliseconds of its previous write, on filesystems with coarse timestamps such as Linux ext4 (#17389 by @will-bogusz)
  • Browser fill in Chrome replaces the text of rich-text editors such as Slate (Discord) and Lexical instead of leaving the old text in place or breaking the editor, and an empty fill clears them (#17417 by @will-bogusz)
  • Requests to the Anthropic API and Factory Droid's hosts now drop their oldest images when long text, tool arguments, or re-declared tool definitions would otherwise push the request past the host's size limit (#17492 by @will-bogusz)
  • Factory Droid requests size images against what each route actually sends: Gemini models count their expanded tool schemas and no longer drop images for another model's reasoning, and only Claude models count withdrawn tool definitions (#17492)

v0.9.99graphify 0.9.99 Stable2026-10-30T23:42:22Z

0.9.99 (2026-10-30)

  • Feat: path when several routes tie on length, graphify path and the MCP shortest_path tool report the most conservative one: among all shortest paths, the route whose weakest hop is weakest is chosen, and the summary notes it was the weakest of N equal-length routes. Previously an arbitrary equal-length route was returned, so the confidence could overstate how sure the connection is. This is the second half of #4881 (the first half, keeping a collapsed edge's weaker evidence in also_seen, shipped in 0.9.98 via #4891, thanks @SyedFahad7).
  • Fix: go a call in a package-level var initialiser (including inside a func-literal closure, the common swappable-hook pattern) is credited to the file node instead of being dropped (#2360, #4867, thanks @nothariharan).
  • Fix: go a method value passed as a function argument (Wrap(s.Health)) is linked as an indirect_call, bringing Go to parity with Python/JS for callback-by-method-value; conservatively guarded against field-access false positives (#1566, #4868, thanks @nothariharan).
  • Fix: go a receiver's field whose struct is declared in a sibling file of the same package is typed, so its member calls resolve across the usual struct-here-methods-there Go layout, and the field types persist across incremental rebuilds (#3368, #4866, thanks @nothariharan).
  • Fix: python module.func values listed in a dispatch table ({"a": mod.func_a}, including nested collections) resolve to the referenced functions as indirect_calls instead of being dropped; non-callable, class, and local-receiver values are left alone (#1566, #4773, thanks @nothariharan).
  • Fix: install gemini gets its own global skill dir (~/.gemini/skills/graphify) on Windows instead of colliding with the agents platform's dir; a pre-existing agents skill is noted, not deleted (#2800, #4770, thanks @nothariharan).
  • Fix: install the global OpenCode plugin is written to ~/.config/opencode (co-located with the global skill) instead of the current directory, with install/uninstall/refresh kept symmetric and legacy locations still cleaned up (#3398, #4771, thanks @nothariharan).
  • Docs: skill the "Follow these steps in order. Do not skip steps." instruction is reworded to "unless the fast path above applies," resolving the contradiction with the existing-graph fast path across all generated hosts (#4061, #4721, thanks @nothariharan).
  • Feat: serve path, explain and neighbors/get_neighbors print an edge's stored confidence_score alongside its tag ([INFERRED 0.75]); EXTRACTED stays bare (1.0 by definition) and a missing or non-finite score keeps the bare tag. Composes with the weakest-hop path summary and the also_seen evidence tags (#4882, #4888, thanks @SyedFahad7).

v0.9.98graphify 0.9.98 Stable2026-10-30T22:55:12Z

0.9.98 (2026-10-30)

  • Fix: build when duplicate same-relation edges collapse, the losing (weaker-confidence) copy's provenance is kept in an also_seen list on the surviving edge instead of being discarded, so the weaker evidence is not silently lost; the field is serialized to graph.json and is idempotent across rebuilds (#4881, #4891, thanks @SyedFahad7).
  • Fix: csharp a C# method node is labelled with its owning type (MyClass.Method) instead of a bare Method, so same-named methods across types are distinguishable; node ids and edges are unchanged (display label only) (#4883, #4889, thanks @SyedFahad7).
  • Feat: path graphify path and the MCP shortest-path output report the overall path confidence as the weakest hop (lowest confidence tier, then lowest score), with a summary line naming that hop (#4885, #4892, thanks @SyedFahad7).
  • Fix: path an endpoint written Type.Member resolves to the member node, not the containing type, so graphify path "Exporter.Run" "PdfReport.Build" finds the real call route; exact names and file names still win first, and a Type.Member whose member does not exist fails closed (#4884, #4893, thanks @SyedFahad7).
  • Fix: extract file ids and per-declaration ids are kept distinct, so a top-level declaration whose name matches its file (for example class Js in a.js) is no longer silently dropped on an id collision; cross-file references bind to the declared id (#4854, #4857, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).
  • Fix: dedup when a cross-file document mention and an AST node collide on a defining id, the AST node keeps the id instead of being dropped, while same-file enrichment, extension twins and single-definer cases are left as-is (#4859, #4872, thanks @TanmayShah29; duplicate approach in #4871 by @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: build a two-file import cycle (a imports b, b imports a) is reported in the default undirected build, and the stamp is cleared correctly on incremental/watch rebuilds so a dropped import no longer leaves a stale cycle (#4839, #4841, thanks @Mpasha17; duplicate approach in #4852 by @legendteddy).
  • Fix: extract a relative JS/TS import carrying a ?query or #fragment suffix (./mod.js?v=1) resolves to the real module instead of a phantom node; Node #subpath imports are left untouched (#4860, #4876, thanks @Jitendarmahara; duplicate approach in #4869 by @mirzasnowy).
  • Fix: go a receiver bound with var x = T{} or var x = &T{} (a composite literal) is typed as T, matching the x := T{} form, so its member calls resolve (#4843, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: verilog a SystemVerilog class constructor (function new(...), which has no return type) gets its own node, method edge and parameter-type references (#4848, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: powershell using module/using assembly drops a real file extension (Helpers.psm1 to helpers) but keeps a dotted module name with no extension intact (Az.Accounts) (#4847, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: solidity a free-function using {a, b} for T set emits uses edges for each named function, not just the single-library using Lib for T form (#4846, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: commonlisp a defclass whose superclass is defined later in the same file binds to that local node instead of minting a sourceless stub (#4845, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: pascal inherited and inline form component blocks (.lfm/.dfm) are recognised, so a later object block keeps its correct parent instead of being re-parented by a corrupted nesting stack (#4844, thanks @ayushcodes10).
  • Fix: serve when two nodes tie in a lookup and differ only by case, the one spelled exactly as queried wins (the others stay reachable one tier down) instead of every spelling being refused as ambiguous (#4870, thanks @nothariharan).
  • Fix: export the Cypher text export keys MERGE on the stable node id and sets the label separately, so re-importing after a label change updates the node instead of creating a duplicate (#4878, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).
  • Fix: pdf the converted-text cache is keyed on the resolved source path, so two PDFs with the same relative name in different roots do not poison each other within one process (#4851, thanks @xunguangzlj-cloud).

Fission-AI/OpenSpec ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v1.16.0v1.16.0 - openspec.dev installs, Node 22 Stable2026-10-30T23:38:25Z

What's New in v1.16.0

Install from openspec.dev, catch more spec mistakes in validate, and a new Node.js floor for npm installs.

Breaking

  • Node.js 22.12.0 or newer for npm installs - Node 20 reached end-of-life on April 30, 2026. The standalone binary, the default install since v1.15.0, doesn't use Node, and Homebrew installs and manages its own Node. If you can't upgrade, switch to the standalone binary: curl -fsSL https://openspec.dev/cli/install.sh | sh (Windows: irm https://openspec.dev/cli/install.ps1 | iex).

New

  • Install from openspec.dev - curl -fsSL https://openspec.dev/cli/install.sh | sh (Windows: irm https://openspec.dev/cli/install.ps1 | iex). Release files are now .tar.gz archives (.zip on Windows).
  • Scenario step check - openspec validate warns when a Scenario: has no WHEN/GIVEN step or no THEN step, in change deltas and main specs. Plain validate and archive are unchanged; --strict fails on it.
  • Store suggestion - When a command finds no OpenSpec root and you have registered stores, the error names the store whose id matches your repo's origin name, with the --store flag and store: line that select it. It only suggests; it never picks a store for you.

Fixed

  • Invalid config.yaml - openspec validate now exits 1 when openspec/config.yaml can't be read or isn't valid YAML, instead of passing while every rule in it is ignored. Other commands still warn and carry on.
  • zsh completion with ZDOTDIR - openspec completion install zsh writes to $ZDOTDIR/.zshrc when ZDOTDIR is an absolute path, the file zsh actually reads. If completion never worked for you, run the install again. completion uninstall zsh also cleans up a block an earlier install left in ~/.zshrc.
  • Inline code fences - A line starting with triple-backtick inline code (```npm test```) no longer opens a phantom code fence that hid every requirement after it.
  • Unspaced headers - validate now reports duplicate or misplaced main-spec requirements written as ###Requirement:, matching how archive reads them.

New Contributors

  • @micromagicman made their first contribution in https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/pull/2077
  • @IvanFeric made their first contribution in https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/pull/2107
  • @artemasmith made their first contribution in https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/pull/2079

Full Changelog: https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/compare/v1.15.0...v1.16.0

(2) The funnel read from outside: search, AI answers from a connected prompt tracker, paid, social and creators, PR, activation, pricing history, referral loops, hiring. (3) Going inside with the user's approval and real identity: sign-up and onboarding screenshots, a 30-60 day email log, the upgrade wall, the cancel flow, the sales process, and a chat-bot probe. (4) Team voices: founders' and leaders' podcasts, talks, and threads, transcribed into dated "reported" claims, plus full job posts read as plans. (5) Hidden signals: DNS (email senders, tool verifications, marketing subdomain platforms), certificate logs for dated subdomain launches, homepage headline history, sitemap growth, paid promotion beyond ad libraries (newsletter, podcast, and YouTube sponsorships, affiliates, coupons, events), and growth counters. (6) Content patterns per channel. (7) Which clusters of moves lined up with growth. (8) The gap with the user's own data. (9) Plays routed to the skill and loop that run each one, with paste-ready prompts. Thirty-one industry packs (SaaS, ecommerce and DTC, consumer hardware, CPG, retail, franchising, local services, residential solar, healthcare, care services, fitness, legal and professional services, real estate, finance, insurance, crypto, gambling, regulated goods, manufacturing, logistics, automotive, govtech, agencies, nonprofit, marketplaces, mobile apps, PC and console games, education, hospitality and travel, events, media and creators), fact-checked against current rules, each with detection signals, growth drivers, signals to collect, first-hand checks, copying limits, plays, and metrics. Teardown, Content, Quick, Funnel Hack (approved-budget purchases, the full money path, upsells, abandoned-cart flows, live tests, paid search conquesting, staged-urgency checks, swipe file), and Watch modes. Bundles scripts/teardown.mjs (zero dependencies): site, stack (98 page-script signatures, matched only in scripts and resource URLs), dns (70+ mail, verification, and platform signatures), history, hero, sitemap-growth, dns, subdomains, detect, shopify, experiments, phones, filings (SEC and Form D), cfpb, fdic, ads, sc-ads (ScrapeCreators), moves, and diff, with contract tests. Fourteen evals.

  • Tools: new ScrapeCreators integration guide for public social posts and ad libraries (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, X, Reddit; Meta, Google, TikTok ads), registered as MCP-enabled. Not used for LinkedIn or people data.

v2.2.5 Stable2026-10-30T23:17:23Z

Highlights

  • Worktree and Shell Mode Shortcuts: Press ⌘⌥O on macOS or Ctrl+Alt+O on Windows and Linux to choose a worktree, and ⌘⌥B or Ctrl+Alt+B to choose its base branch. ⌘⇧X or Ctrl+Shift+X now toggles shell mode in the composer. (#60713)
  • Send Quotes From the Comment Popup: Hold ⌘ or Ctrl in the quote popup to turn its checkmark into send, or press ⌘Enter or Ctrl+Enter, to send just that quote and comment while leaving the rest of the composer untouched. (#60640)
  • Percentage Compaction Buffer: Set "compaction": { "buffer": "20%" } in opencode.json to keep a share of each model's context window free, so one setting fits models with small and large windows. Token counts still work. (#60647)

Core

Improvements

  • compaction.buffer accepts a percentage of the model's context window, such as "20%", in addition to a token count. (#60647)
  • When read misses because a folder is missing, the error names that folder and the nearest one that exists. (#60688)
  • When edit can't find oldString, the error shows the file's closest lines, or says the change is already there. (#60689)
  • Calls to a tool named bash now run as shell instead of failing, with the same permissions. A plugin tool actually named bash still takes precedence. (#60687)

Bug fixes

  • MCP servers that send stdio messages larger than 10 MiB no longer get disconnected, and large messages are read much faster. (#60694)
  • Idle locations no longer restart their MCP servers right after shutting down. (#60668)
  • Compaction now caps its prompt at the model's context window when the input limit is larger. (#60660)
  • LiteLLM context window errors now trigger compaction instead of stopping the session. (#60692)
  • Reasoning is no longer turned into plain text when you switch models or resume an interrupted response, which caused request errors on some providers. (#60498)

TUI

Bug fixes

  • The connect menu no longer lists MCP servers, which are managed in their own place. (#60675)

Desktop

Improvements

  • Added keyboard shortcuts to choose a worktree and its base branch, shown in tooltips, and a shortcut to toggle shell mode. The worktree path can be selected to copy the full directory. (#60713)
  • Hold ⌘ or Ctrl in the quote popup to send a quote and its comment directly. (#60640)
  • Added flat input surfaces and a compact input size. (#60598)

Bug fixes

  • The connect menu no longer lists MCP servers. (#60675)
  • Added the missing top inset to the search field in the recently closed menu. (#60652)

View release →

v2.2.4 Stable2026-10-30T16:59:08Z

Highlights

  • Persistent Desktop Terminals: Desktop terminals now belong to the session, survive server restarts with their scrollback, and stay synchronized with the TUI and other windows. Renamed terminals also keep their names across restarts. (#60346)
  • Publish Interactive Artifacts: Enable "experimental": { "artifacts": true } in opencode.json to let agents publish, update, and serve HTML or static artifacts through the built-in local provider or plugin-provided storage. (#60351)
  • Guided Claude Agent Setup: Select Claude Agent from the provider picker to copy claude auth login, install Claude Code, and verify the connection before continuing to model selection. (#60603)
  • Choose a Base Branch Quickly: While creating a worktree, open Choose base branch with ⌘⌥. on macOS or Ctrl+Alt+. on Windows and Linux. The command is also available in the command palette and Settings › Shortcuts. (#60579)

Core

Improvements

  • Added opt-in artifacts with artifact_create, artifact_read, artifact_update, and artifact_delete, including a built-in local static-file provider. (#60351)
  • Made enabled schedules run under opencode serve and coordinated multiple server processes so a schedule fires only once. Schedules remain opt-in through experimental.schedules. (#60478)
  • Raised OpenCode Go limits for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. (#60625)

Bug fixes

  • Allowed user, project, and remote configuration to override Console-supplied provider names, limits, variants, settings, and headers. (#60597)
  • Kept local OpenCode service requests out of environment-configured proxies. (#60441)
  • Replaced Claude Code’s misleading /login instruction with claude auth login. Thanks @Tarquinen. (#60592)

TUI

Bug fixes

  • Preserved prompt cursor styles applied by plugins when themes or unrelated prompt state change. (#60599)
  • Added missing right padding to edit and patch diffs. (#60614)
  • Extended the vertical session-tab activity pulse across the full tab width. (#60338)

Desktop

Improvements

  • Moved terminals to persistent session PTYs shared with the TUI and other windows, with restored scrollback, server-side renaming, and restart persistence. (#60346)
  • Added guided Claude Agent installation, sign-in, connection checking, and recovery from Needs sign-in. (#60603)
  • Added Choose base branch to the command palette and shortcuts, bound to ⌘⌥. or Ctrl+Alt+.. (#60579)
  • Simplified the session location popover and made long paths easier to read. (#60492)

Bug fixes

  • Kept terminal tab clicks and rename fields attached to the intended tab. (#60645)
  • Listed matching commands before sessions in command-palette search. (#60616)
  • Restored copying user messages from an open actions menu. (#60576)
  • Reduced repeated work and allocations while streaming Markdown, especially in long sessions. (#60549, #60562, #60577)

SDK

Improvements

  • Added client.experimental.artifacts.providers, list, create, get, update, delete, and view. (#60351)
  • Extended client.experimental.persistentPty.update to rename terminals or clear a user title, and exposed userTitle plus persistent-pty.updated events. (#60329)

Extensions

Improvements

  • Added ctx.experimental.artifact.transform(...) to Effect and Promise plugins for registering artifact providers, capabilities, prompts, and the default provider. (#60351)

thedotmack/claude-mem ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v15.7.0 Stable2026-10-30T18:18:54Z

My Work: refresh stays on your agent, and a Feedback button (#5190)

When My Work's automatic refresh got an answer from Claude Code that claude-mem refused (most often a review over 1,200 characters), the whole refresh moved on to the next logged-in agent. On machines with Codex installed, that meant hidden codex exec --ephemeral runs on the owner's ChatGPT account, even with CLAUDE_MEM_PROVIDER=claude (#5189: about 230 runs in four days).

  • A refused answer now ends that refresh on the agent that gave it. The next scheduled run tries the same agent again, with the existing failure backoff. An agent that can't run at all (not signed in, crashed) still hands the run to the next one.
  • Feedback button in the My Work header, next to Star. It opens a short "My Work feedback" issue form.

Note-taker always uses the newest Haiku (#5195)

The note-taker's default model is now Claude Code's haiku alias, which always resolves to the newest Haiku, instead of a pinned Haiku 4.5 ID. Saved settings that still carry the shipped pinned ID move to the alias on upgrade. A model you typed yourself is left alone. The repo's CLAUDE.md now states this as policy: never pin a dated model ID as a default.

My Work and the worker

  • Activity-driven background rebuilds of My Work are coalesced, so an open My Work page no longer rebuilds on every database commit (#5133, mitigates #5124).
  • Work View waits for the database to finish starting before it builds (#5157).
  • The viewer's processing status reconciles after a stream gap (#5139).
  • Daily worker logs older than CLAUDE_MEM_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS (default 30, 0 keeps forever) are pruned. Today's and yesterday's files are always kept (#5186).

Projects

  • Named environments inside a parent Git repository can declare explicit inheritance, so unrelated parent memory no longer leaks into their context (#5022).
  • Oh My Pi keeps transient project memory in model context (#5183).
  • Claude Duet: capture and recall (#5188).

Media (off by default)

  • First phase of image-aware observations: bounded media contracts and a lazy Sharp 0.35.5 converter with size, pixel and deadline limits. CLAUDE_MEM_MEDIA_CAPTURE_ENABLED and CLAUDE_MEM_MEDIA_INFERENCE_ENABLED both default to false (#4341).

Security

  • Executable discovery never looks in the current directory (#5148).
  • Installer URLs are https, and Bun runs from an owner-controlled directory (#5149).
  • The worker rejects cross-origin browser writes to session endpoints and to POST /api/memory/ingest (#5162, #5161).
  • Postgres API keys are stored as salted scrypt hashes (#5160), and every Postgres sslmode is honored (#5152).
  • Atomic writes use exclusive-create random temp names (#5151).
  • Private tags are stripped before caps, and Hermes' last turn is gated (#5150).
  • Redaction now covers GitLab, Hugging Face and npm tokens (#5174), passwords in URL credentials (#5173), and inbound sync text when local redaction is on (#5171).

Fixes

  • Hook stdin is framed when complete, without waiting for EOF (#5126).
  • A closed session's EPIPE is no longer logged as fatal (#5177).
  • Windows Codex sandbox refusals are explained (#5140).
  • The OpenAI-compatible provider reads the HTTP status from a 200 error envelope with a textual code (#5191).
  • SessionStart counts the memory-use block in its budget without TeamBrain (#5181).
  • A leading ~ in CLAUDE_MEM_DATA_DIR is expanded (#5179).
  • Log tails read only complete lines (#5166).
  • The filtered Chroma fallback narrows to SQLite row ids (#5154).

Full changelog: https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/compare/v15.6.0...v15.7.0
